parentIntro: This is THE week of the year for her — the placement diagnostic found exactly one gap, and it was multi-digit subtraction (she missed 42 − 27 and 407 − 10). Her number bonds are strong, so the facts aren't the problem: choosing a road is. Three roads this week — COUNT UP for numbers close together, JUMP BACK for taking away a chunk, and ROUND-AND-PAY-BACK for near-hundreds.
watchFor: Two things. The “2 take away 7” panic when the top digit is smaller — head it off with a number line before she freezes. And zeros: 300 − 156 and 604 − 8 are the ones that catch her out. Praise the CHOICE of road out loud and separately from the answer — that's the habit we're actually building this week.

demo.title: Three roads to a take-away
demo.say: Take-aways are the thing you and I have been working on all year. Today, three different roads — and the clever bit is picking the right one.

steps.caption: these two are far apart… but not that far
steps.say: Three hundred and forty two, take away one hundred and fifty six. Let's count UP from the smaller one and see how big the gap is.

steps.caption: count up in friendly hops
steps.say: From one fifty six, four gets us to a hundred and sixty. Then a hundred and forty gets us to three hundred. Then forty two more to three hundred and forty two.

steps.caption: add the hops — that's the answer
steps.say: Now add up all the hops. Four, plus a hundred and forty, plus forty two. One hundred and eighty six!

steps.caption: add it back to prove it
steps.say: And here's how we know we're right. Put it back: one fifty six plus one eighty six gives three hundred and forty two. It fits!

weDo.model: Empty number line. Put 138 at the left end and 254 at the right. She decides the hops; you only draw what she tells you.
steps: Ask: “are these two numbers close together or far apart?” (Fairly close — so counting up is the fast road.)
Hop to a friendly number first: 138 → 140 is 2. Then 140 → 250 is 110. Then 250 → 254 is 4.
Check by adding back: 138 + 116 = 254. Ask her to say why that check works.

weDo.model: Number line again. 99 is desperate to be 100 — and this is where subtraction plays a trick on you.
steps: Ask what friendly number 99 is nearly (100), then do the easy sum: 234 − 100 = 134.
Now the golden question: “we took away ONE TOO MANY — so do we give it back, or take more away?”
Let her reason it out with the number line. Taking away too much means we owe her one: 134 + 1 = 135.
Compare with last week's adding trick, where you paid one BACK. Ask why they go opposite ways — this is the bit that makes her think.

What is one thousand take away two hundred and fifty?
